Every assertion round 5 added can fail. Seven mutations, each run against `scripts/test_account_workflows.py` alone on a restored tree: `buf_m`->`buf_t` (2 failed); `.strip()` terminator (1 failed); assignment branch without `_one_command` (2 failed); `_UNMODELLED` emptied (1 failed); `_pattern_end` returning the whole line (1 failed); a bucket string typo'd to `guardedd` (reds test_every_command_gets_one_of_the_four_answers); `_model_strip_then_mask`'s continuation backslash reverted to a blank (reds test_every_rejected_model_reads_a_backslash_as_the_scanner_does).
Count and exit code verified myself, twice, on a clean tree at 6d82eb0: 1224 passed, EXIT=0, ~101s. `git status --short` empty before and after every mutation.

No other `_carved_out` branch has the *prefix* weakness in its original form: `_STRUCTURE`, `_CASE_OPEN` and `_COMPOUND_HEAD` are anchored at both ends (or use `\b`), and `set -uo pipefail` / `:` / `}` are exact-string comparisons. The weakness survives in two other costumes - see defects 1 and 4.

defects.summary: `_carved_out`'s assignment branch admits a VARIABLE-ASSIGNMENT PREFIX to an arbitrary command. `FOO=bar mkdir -p ../scratch` is one simple command, so `_one_command` says yes, `_ASSIGNMENT` matches at the start, and the whole thing is carved out - the same prefix-match defect round 5 was sent to close on that exact branch, in its third costume.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1987. `_ASSIGNMENT` is `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=`, anchored only at the start; `_one_command` rejects `|`, `&` and `;` and nothing else - and a `NAME=value cmd` prefix contains none of them, because in shell grammar it IS a simple command. Measured: `_carved_out('FOO=bar mkdir -p /proc/nope/child')` is True, `_carved_out('LC_ALL=C false')` is True, `_carved_out('x=1 y=2 mkdir -p /proc/nope/child')` is True, and all three abort under `set -uo pipefail` + `bash -e` with `reached` never printed. End to end: `self._with_lines_before_the_case(['FOO=bar mkdir -p ../scratch'])` on the real .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml is clean under `bash -n` and the guard SILENTLY PASSES - no red anywhere in the class. It survives every wrapper I tried (plain, inside a `case` arm, inside an `if` body, inside an `else`, inside a brace group, after a continuation, after a `::warning::`): 7 of 7 silent. The carve-out list at scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1898-1907 says the entry is for `a bare assignment - harness_ok=yes, verdict="${verdict#...}"` and that it must be `A SIMPLE COMMAND`; `FOO=bar mkdir` satisfies the letter of that sentence and defeats its intent, so the comment is the wrong shape to fix it with. `_NOT_A_SIMPLE_ASSIGNMENT` (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:2430) tests only the `|` and `&` shapes, so nothing in the suite reaches this.

defects.summary: `_classify_region` marks EVERYTHING textually left of the final `&&`/`||` as `guarded` in one blob, without splitting it at top-level `;`. Any `;`-separated list whose last pair is guarded silently exempts every command before that final `;` - and the blob also bypasses the `_UNMODELLED` and inline-`case` raises, which sit only in the `;` loop below it.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:2043-2047: `guards = _top_level(mask, ("||", "&&")); at, token = guards[-1]; classified.append((start, text[:at].strip(), "guarded"))`. The `;` split at line 2049 runs only on what is LEFT AFTER the guard, so the left-hand text is never split at all. Measured on the real step: splicing `mkdir -p ../scratch ; echo hi || echo bye` above `case "$verdict" in` is clean under `bash -n` and the guard SILENTLY PASSES; `_classified()` returns exactly two entries for it - `(248, 'mkdir -p ../scratch ; echo hi', 'guarded')` and `(248, 'echo bye', 'carved-out')`. Bash disagrees: `mkdir -p /proc/nope/child ; echo hi || echo bye` under `set -uo pipefail` + `bash -e` exits non-zero with `reached` never printed. Same silence for `mkdir -p ../scratch ; echo hi && echo bye`, for `echo a ; mkdir -p ../scratch ; echo hi || echo bye`, for `: ; mkdir -p ../scratch ; : || :`, and inside a `case` arm (`zzz) echo a ; mkdir -p ../scratch ; echo hi || echo bye`) - 14 silent passes across my wrapper x payload sweep, all this one root cause. The class docstring gets the rule right in words - 'Errexit's exemption covers the command BEFORE the final `&&`/`||`', singular - and `_classified`'s docstring then states the implemented version as if it were the same thing: 'the left of the final `&&`/`||`'. It is not: errexit exempts one command, not a whole `;` list. `test_a_command_after_the_final_or_aborts_the_step_too` executes three shapes (`after-a-||`, `bare`, `before-a-||`) and none of them is `A ; B || C`, so the executed table never measures the half that is wrong. Latent in the shipped step today (no logical line has a top-level `;` left of a final guard) - which is the same status the three round-4 blocking defects had.

defects.summary: `_strip_heredocs` reads a heredoc opener off `_uncomment`'s output, which strips COMMENTS but not QUOTED STRINGS - so `<<PY` inside a `::warning::` string opens a heredoc, and because the step already has a real `PY` terminator, everything between is silently blanked. Both the guard and its own coverage control pass, and `assert delim is None` never fires. This is the here-string defect of round 4, unfixed for the quoted case.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:763 - `opener = _HEREDOC_OPENER.search(_uncomment(line))`; `_uncomment` (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:255-310) returns the line with only the comment removed, quotes intact. Measured against the REAL body: inserting `echo "::warning::the verdict block <<PY could not be read"` plus `mkdir -p ../scratch` immediately above `pip_ok=yes` (line 52) leaves `bash -n` clean; `test_every_command_that_can_fail_sits_in_an_if_or_an_or_list` SILENTLY PASSES, `test_the_classifier_reads_every_line_of_the_step` PASSES, and `_classified()` drops from 59 commands to 55 - the mkdir, the pip install, the `verdict=$(python3 - <<'PY'` capture and its guard all vanish, because the real `PY` on line 78 is now read as the false opener's terminator. Minimal reproduction: `echo "see <<EOF later" / mkdir -p /proc/nope/child / EOF / echo done` - bash prints `see <<EOF later` then aborts on the mkdir (exit 1), while `_strip_heredocs` returns that same body with the mkdir line blanked to spaces. The single-quoted form `echo 'x <<EOF y'` is silent too. `_strip_heredocs`' round-5 docstring (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:735-745) states the opposite as a general rule - 'the assertion closes the consequence of reading an opener where there is none, because a word that is not a delimiter is a word no later line equals' - and names only the comment case ('The opener is read off `_uncomment`'s output so a `<<` inside a comment cannot start one'). A word inside a quoted string is exactly a word a later line CAN equal, and in this step one already does.

defects.summary: `_OUTPUT_WRITE`'s `.*` admits an arbitrary EXTRA redirect before the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` append, so `echo hi > <failing path> >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` is carved out as 'the one deliberately unguarded failable command' and passes silently while aborting the step for a different reason.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1932 - `_OUTPUT_WRITE = re.compile(r'^echo\s+.*>>\s*"\$GITHUB_OUTPUT"$')`. `_headed_by` now guarantees a simple command, so the pipeline hole is closed, but nothing bounds what sits between `echo` and the append. Measured: `_carved_out('echo hi > /proc/nope/zz >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"')` is True and `_OUTPUT_WRITE.match(...)` is True; the same command under `set -uo pipefail` + `bash -e` aborts with `reached` never printed. `echo hi 2> /proc/nope/zz >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` behaves identically. End to end: splicing `echo hi > ../scratch/zz >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` above the real `case` is clean under `bash -n` and the guard SILENTLY PASSES. The carve-out list (scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1918-1923) justifies the entry as 'There is no degraded path when the runner cannot write its own output file' - a failure on some OTHER file is not that case, and the bullet's own hedge names only pipelines ('a pipeline ending in that redirect is not the write this describes').

defects.summary: The workflow prose round 4 was flagged for is still there and is now false in a new way: it says the carve-out 'takes a pipeline as the command it ends with', and after round 5 no pipeline is ever carved out at all. The fix report records this defect's doc half as resolved, but the five commits touch only `scripts/test_account_workflows.py`.
defects.evidence: .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml:206-207 - '...which matches a command's NAME rather than its first four letters, and takes a pipeline as the command it ends with.' `git diff --name-only HEAD~5` returns exactly one path, `scripts/test_account_workflows.py`, so the sentence is byte-identical to the one round 4 reported. Measured against the code it describes: `_carved_out('grep -q x /etc/hostname | echo hi')` is False, `_carved_out('true | echo done')` is False, `_carved_out('echo hi | grep -q zzz')` is False - `_one_command` rejects any `|` outright and never evaluates what the pipeline ends with. A reader following the sentence would expect a pipeline ending in `echo` to be exempt; it reds. AGENTS.md's rule for this repo is that no comment may assert what a reader cannot check - this one asserts something a reader CAN check, and it is wrong.

defects.summary: `_classify_region`'s compound-head assertion fires on ordinary bash that puts `then`/`do` on its own line, and the sentence it fails with says the opposite of what the code does.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:2031-2038. `if true` / `then` / `  mkdir -p ../scratch` / `fi` is valid bash and `bash -n` accepts it, but `head` is `if true`, which matches `_COMPOUND_HEAD` and ends in neither `then` nor `do`, so the guard raises: 'line 248 of the audit step opens a compound command and puts something after its `then`/`do` on the same line'. There is nothing after its `then`/`do`; the line has no `then` at all. Loud rather than silent, so not a pass - but a maintainer who writes the conventional two-line form gets a red whose explanation is checkably false, which is the failure mode the `stillOpen` note about `for`/`!`/`time` already anticipates for the `bare` bucket and does not cover here. Either widen `_COMPOUND_HEAD`'s handling to a head continued on the next line, or make the message say what it actually detected (a compound head this classifier cannot bracket).
